provenance.what: Wall-clock cost of one full five-game Atari run, seed 0, single GPU.
provenance.source: report/figures/compute_cost_wall.svg, the rendered figure built by report/gen_figures.py::fig_compute_cost. The underlying run directories (results/atari5_v5_order2_seed0, the three CLEAR sweep runs, atari5_joint_6m_seed0) are gitignored and live only on the cluster, so the values are cached here.
provenance.measurement_caveat: THE TWO SERIES ARE MEASURED DIFFERENTLY and the comparison is indicative, not exact. Ours sums per-phase wall_s (task1 + local + global) from resource_usage.json, which counts only time inside the training phases. CLEAR and Joint take t_wall from the last row of logs.jsonl, which is total elapsed and therefore also includes evaluation, checkpointing and setup. Ours is the number that is understated by this, so the gap shown is a lower bound on ours' advantage, not an inflated one.
provenance.seeds: Single seed. No error bars are drawn and none are invented.
provenance.note_on_existing_figure: report/manifest.json currently captions compute_cost_wall as 'V5 is substantially slower than CLEAR'. That contradicts its own data (15.1 h and 18.1 h against 36.4-37.3 h). The caption is stale; the numbers below are read from the figure itself.

_ours_note: The min-max run on the task order used throughout this report.
_clear_note: Across the CLEAR replay-buffer configurations, which land within 0.9 h of one another (36.4, 36.9, 37.3).
_joint_note: The budget-matched jointly-trained model, 6M frames per game.
